header.name: Operating Systems
header.description: Operating system is the interface between the hardware and the user; it is responsible for the management and coordination of activities and the sharing of the resources of the computer. Operating system offers a number of services to application programs and users. Applications access these services through application programming interfaces (APIs) or system calls. By invoking these interfaces, the application can request a service from the operating system, pass parameters, and receive the results of the operation. The course on Operating System has two components: theory and programming. Theory component covers the underline concepts and principles of operating system whereas programming component involves the practical implementation of theoretical concepts.

cos.label: CO1
cos.text: Students are able to create a Unix shell with complete clarity about process creation and process execution.

cos.label: CO2
cos.text: Students are able to write multi- threaded applications with synchronization primitives and ability to analyze effects of concurrency on process execution and correctness.

cos.label: CO3
cos.text: Students are able to analyze the impact of OS concepts, e.g. virtual memory, concurrency, on program execution and ability to fine-tune the program to run efficiently on a given OS.

cos.label: CO4
cos.text: Students are able to demonstrate deeper understanding of the Unix-like OSes and kernel programming.

lecture_weeks.topic_raw: x86/x86_64 architecture, compiler tool chain, writing C/Assembly mixed programs
Process and thread management - creation, deletion, waiting, context switching, relevant system calls and their implementations
lecture_weeks.tutorial: Rudimentary shell using process creation and management, kernel programming - writing your own system call
Synchronization primitives and using appropriate system calls.
Kernel scheduler programming - Modifying the kernel CFS scheduler

lecture_weeks.topic_raw: Page fault and page fault handling
lecture_weeks.tutorial: Programming assignments - Memory management unit in OS

lecture_weeks.topic_raw: File system: File system management, VFS, file allocation/file system
I/O management , device drivers, kernel modules
lecture_weeks.tutorial: Programming assignments - File system, device driver
